teaser.text: Tesco PLC is a retailer built around everyday shopping, from a full supermarket trip to a quick local purchase. It earns money by moving a huge volume of goods and services through stores, websites and business relationships while keeping only a small part as operating profit.

stock.title: Tesco stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Tesco’s stock forecast weighs bear, base and bull cases against cash generation, margins, valuation and shareholder returns.
stock.opening: Tesco’s weighted scenario reaches 600.95p in October 2029. It hinges on cash-and-margin execution.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Tesco’s business works, who its rivals are, how its management allocates capital, and what risks could change the path.

blocks.heading: Where could Tesco’s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: Tesco’s probability-weighted path points to moderate returns, with considerable risk around the central case. The forecast gives weighted prices of 549.60p in October 2027, 573.66p in October 2028 and 600.95p in October 2029, equal to returns including dividends of 11%, 19% and 28%. Today’s reference price is 508.20p. By October 2029, the bear-to-bull range runs from 333.43p to 923.86p.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Tesco, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear row falls from £1,850m to £1,799m as revenue grows only 2% and margin compresses to 2.30%. The bull row rises from £2,300m to £2,653m as 4% revenue growth combines with margins reaching 3.20%. The bear reflects thin margins, price competition and wage pressure; the bull requires share gains, Clubcard engagement, better online density and automation to outweigh those costs.
Tesco’s upside is a cash-and-margin execution story, not simply a sales-growth story.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Tesco really make?

paragraphs.text: Tesco must maintain stores, refrigeration, vehicles, warehouses and software. Capital spending reached £1,660m, while lease payments were £667m. A broader calculation produced free cash flow of £1,393m. Tesco reported £1,957m under its own definition, which treats some property and adjusting payments differently.

Share-based pay is also an economic cost because employees receive ownership that would otherwise belong to existing shareholders. Deducting £105m produced an analytical real free cash flow of £1,288m, or 19.50p per diluted share. This is not a separate statutory cash line, and careless adjustments can count some share-related cash costs twice.

dividend.meta_description: Tesco's dividend has risen in the supplied record and is supported by cash generation, while investment and shareholder returns compete for cash.
dividend.opening: Tesco pays a dividend per share that has increased each year in the supplied record, with the latest completed-year dividend at £0.145. Tesco generates substantial cash, but coverage depends on what remains after normal working capital, necessary investment and recurring obligations.
dividend.closing: The full memo also covers Tesco's business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Tesco pay per share over the years shown?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise gradually in the base case, from £0.153 to £0.169 per share. The bear case holds at £0.145, matching the latest completed-year dividend. The bull case rises from £0.158 to £0.187. Tesco has increased its dividend each year in the supplied record and targets a progressive policy near 50% of adjusted EPS, while the newly declared interim is 5.05p.

blocks.heading: Does Tesco's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: The pattern matters more than any single year. Tesco repaid debt during the first four years, then raised a small amount of net debt in the latest year. Acquisitions absorbed little across the period, while exceptional money from the banking disposal supported an additional buyback of about £700 million.

That explains how distributions could exceed one year’s free cash flow without proving that Tesco financed the whole gap with new borrowing. The company could also use cash accumulated earlier or proceeds from selling a business. Debt repayment improved resilience, but recurring dividends and buybacks still need recurring cash after necessary reinvestment.

paragraphs.text: Management guides to group adjusted operating profit of £3,150m–£3,300m and free cash flow of £1,500m–£2,000m for the year to February 2027. Capital expenditure of approximately £1,700m and a £950m buyback will compete with dividends and other uses of cash. Tesco also targets £500m of Save to Invest savings and a £500m Whoosh sales milestone; neither target is additional profit.

blocks.heading: What is Tesco's dividend yield against its price?

paragraphs.text: Cash measures complete the picture. A 6.1% free-cash-flow yield compares cash generation with the share price, while a 2.9% dividend yield measures the cash dividend. But first-half free cash flow of £1.57 billion benefited from about £250 million of payroll timing, which was expected to reverse. The investor therefore needs repeatable operating cash after investment, interest, tax and leases.
